successCriteria.description: The `LeaveBalance` interface is exported from `src/modules/balance/balance.model.ts` with all canonical fields: `id: string`, `employeeId: string`, `policyId: string`, `totalEntitlement: number`, `usedDays: number`, `remainingDays: number`, `fiscalYear: number`, `status: 'ACTIVE' | 'EXHAUSTED' | 'FROZEN'`, `createdAt: Date`, `updatedAt: Date`.

The `IBalanceRepository` interface is exported from `src/modules/balance/balance.repository.ts` with all six methods: `findById`, `findByEmployeeAndPolicy`, `findByEmployeeAndFiscalYear`, `create`, `update`, and `updateUsedDays` — each with the exact signatures specified in the phase scope.

`BalanceRepository` implements `IBalanceRepository` and uses the shared `pool` from `src/shared/db/connection.ts` as its default database connection, with an optional `Pool | PoolClient` constructor parameter for transaction support.
`BalanceRepository.create` persists a new row in the `leave_balances` table and returns the created `LeaveBalance` with `id`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt` populated by the database.
`BalanceRepository.updateUsedDays` atomically sets `usedDays` and `remainingDays` on the identified row and returns the updated `LeaveBalance`, or `null` if the row does not exist.
`BalanceRepository.findByEmployeeAndFiscalYear` returns all balances for the given employee and fiscal year as an array (empty array when none exist).

Jest unit tests exist in `tests/unit/modules/balance/` covering all six repository methods: success cases, null/empty returns, and the custom-client constructor path — following the same mock-pool pattern established by `tests/unit/modules/policy/policy.repository.test.ts`.

constraints: All database access must go through the repository layer — no inline SQL or direct pool usage outside `BalanceRepository` (GP-001).

The `BalanceRepository` constructor must accept an optional `Pool | PoolClient` parameter defaulting to the shared `pool` from `src/shared/db/connection.ts`, matching the pattern in `EmployeeRepository` and `PolicyRepository` (Transaction Contract from reconciled architecture).

SQL column names must use `snake_case`; the private row-mapping helper must convert to `camelCase` TypeScript properties — matching the convention in `EmployeeRepository.rowToEmployee` and `PolicyRepository.rowToPolicy`.

The `updateUsedDays` method must accept an optional `PoolClient` (via the constructor-injected client) so a caller's transaction can atomically update status and balance together — as required by the Transaction Contract in the reconciled architecture.

entityInvariants.invariant: `remainingDays` must always equal `totalEntitlement - usedDays` — the repository is not required to enforce this arithmetically (the service layer owns that), but any persisted row must satisfy this invariant.

`status` must be one of `'ACTIVE'`, `'EXHAUSTED'`, or `'FROZEN'`. `EXHAUSTED` is reached when `remainingDays === 0`. The repository does not enforce the transition — the service layer owns lifecycle — but the type system must restrict the field to these three literals.

The tuple `(employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear)` is unique — at most one balance row may exist for a given employee, policy, and fiscal year. The database enforces this via a unique constraint on `(employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year)`.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns `null` when no row matches the given `id` — never throws for a missing row.
Returns `null` when no balance exists for the given employee-policy pair — never throws for a missing row.
